finding.expected: Normalize and classify the PowerShell call-operator form before git policy evaluation. A leading & followed by a quoted or unquoted git/git.exe executable path must be treated as the same git invocation category. Bounded inspection/terminalization forms may remain allowed; destructive/history-changing/network/unknown forms must deny with AIOS_GIT_OPERATION_NOT_ADMITTED; diff --check in any benign ordering must deny with AIOS_RUNTIME_OWNS_VERIFICATION. Add regressions for safe and destructive & "C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe" forms and for an absolute unquoted git.exe path where syntactically applicable. Do not widen generic shell execution.
finding.issue: The final guard now handles bare/path-prefixed git, quoted executable tokens, inspection-only branch forms, and chains that begin directly with a recognized git token, but it still does not fail closed for the normal PowerShell call-operator form required to execute a quoted Windows executable path. _normalize_git_invocation() only classifies commands whose first executable token itself is git/git.exe. Therefore a command such as & "C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe" push origin main or & "C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe" reset --hard HEAD begins with the PowerShell call operator &, is not classified as git, is not a trailing-background-marker case, and falls through the generic allow path. This leaves a Windows-specific bypass of the task's explicit git-category fail-closed requirement for quoted/absolute Windows executable paths.
